headline_marked: Miss World Bangladesh [[launches nationwide hygiene campaign]]
headline: Miss World Bangladesh launches nationwide hygiene campaign
summary: The 'Hygiene for Health Bangladesh' initiative aims to prevent disease through simple everyday habits, supported by the government and various NGOs.
details: Miss World Bangladesh 2026 Samanzar Sayeed has launched a nationwide hygiene awareness campaign titled 'Hygiene for Health Bangladesh'. The initiative focuses on promoting hygiene as a simple and effective way to prevent disease across the country.
The campaign was officially launched at Gulshan Society Lake Park in Gulshan-2, in partnership with the Gulshan Society and with government support.

Health Minister Sardar Md Sakhawat Husain praised the initiative, stating that hygiene is one of the most cost-effective tools for preventing disease and reminding that public health starts with simple habits.
The project reflects the 'Beauty With a Purpose' philosophy of the Miss World pageant, encouraging titleholders to champion social causes alongside their ambassadorial roles.
The campaign will mobilise youth volunteers to conduct educational and community outreach programmes to spread awareness about hygiene practices.

The initiative is supported by a wide range of partners, including the Dhaka North City Corporation, Manusher Jonno Foundation, Friendship, and several educational institutions and corporate sponsors.
The launch event concluded with the symbolic release of biodegradable balloons and pigeons, and the opening of registration for nationwide volunteers.
Samanzar Sayeed is set to represent Bangladesh at the Miss World 2026 grand finale in Nha Trang, Vietnam, on September 5.

headline_marked: Global energy alert: [[QatarEnergy to extend LNG supply halt]] through mid-October
headline: Global energy alert: QatarEnergy to extend LNG supply halt through mid-October
summary: The move comes as shipping in the Strait of Hormuz slows significantly due to escalating tensions between Tehran and Washington.
details: QatarEnergy is preparing to extend a force majeure on liquefied natural gas (LNG) shipments, potentially lasting through mid-October, according to a Bloomberg News report.
Several LNG buyers across Europe and Asia are reportedly expecting formal notifications regarding the extension of the supply halt.
The disruption is linked to the near-halt of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical maritime corridor where all of Qatar's LNG exports transit.
Qatar currently accounts for approximately 20% of global LNG exports, making any prolonged supply disruption a significant risk to global energy markets.
The shipping slowdown in the Strait of Hormuz is attributed to escalating tensions between Tehran and Washington.
Force majeure is a legal clause that exempts parties from liability when they cannot meet supply obligations due to events beyond their control.
